findings.title: POST /api/waterings returns 500 for NaN or Infinity litres
findings.steps: Signed in, POST {"bed_id":1,"litres":NaN} or {"bed_id":1,"litres":Infinity} (Python's JSON parser accepts these literals)
findings.evidence: curl: 'Internal Server Error [500]' for both payloads; 1e308 correctly gives 422

findings.title: Huge bed_id or watering id causes 500 instead of 4xx
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error (SQLite integer overflow); the page with ?bed=99999999999999999999 shows a generic error
findings.evidence: All three answered 'Internal Server Error [500]'. bed_id has gt=0 but no upper bound

findings.title: Small litre amounts are accepted but shown as '0 L'
findings.where: Beds page past-watering form / POST /api/waterings, dashboard and Waterings page
findings.steps: Record a past watering with litres 0.001 (the form has novalidate, so step/min don't stop it; the API accepts it)
findings.expected: Refuse amounts below the 0.1 step with a reason, or show the real value
findings.actual: Saved, then listed as '0 L' on the dashboard and Waterings page
findings.evidence: API returned 201 with litres 0.001; the dashboard HTML shows 'North bed 0 L'

findings.title: Absurd past dates accepted (e.g. year 0001)
findings.expected: Refuse implausible dates with a visible reason (only the future is checked)
findings.actual: 201 Created; the bed's history/log shows a watering in year 1

findings.title: Invalid bed filter shows a raw internal field message
findings.steps: Open /waterings?bed=abc (for example from an edited or old link)
findings.expected: A readable message or ignore the bad filter, with the filter control in sync
findings.actual: Alert reads 'Query.bed id: Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer'; the bed select shows no selected option
findings.evidence: SSR HTML: <div class="alert alert--error">Query.bed id: Input should be a valid integer...

findings.title: Load errors on Waterings page and dashboard 'Recent waterings' offer no retry
findings.steps: Make GET /api/waterings fail (server down or 5xx), open the page
findings.expected: An error state with a Retry button that refetches without a reload
findings.actual: Only an AlertMessage is shown; index.vue never destructures refresh for the waterings fetch, and waterings.vue has no retry control. The only way to recover is a reload (or changing the filter on /waterings)
findings.evidence: index.vue: `const { data: waterings, error: wateringsError } = wateringsResult` with no refresh; the waterings.vue template has no retry button

findings.title: Bed list failure on Waterings page is silent; filter just shows 'All beds'
findings.expected: A visible error saying the bed filter could not load, with a retry
findings.actual: bedsResult.error is ignored; the select only has 'All beds', which looks like the garden has no beds
findings.evidence: waterings.vue: `const { data: beds } = bedsResult`, and the error is never rendered

findings.title: No request timeout: 'Water now'/'Save watering'/delete can spin forever
findings.steps: Make the API stall (accept the connection but never respond), then click 'Water now'
findings.expected: Fails after 10 s with a visible error, and the button re-enables
findings.actual: useApiClient/useApiFetch set no timeout, so the button stays on 'Watering…'/'Saving…' and disabled indefinitely, and loading text stays forever
findings.evidence: composables/useApi.ts $fetch.create has no timeout option; grep for 'timeout' in frontend finds nothing

findings.title: Recording a watering is not idempotent: a retry after timeout or failure creates duplicates
findings.steps: Click 'Save watering'; the request reaches the server but the response is lost or slow; the user clicks again
findings.actual: Each POST inserts a new row, and there is no idempotency key or client request id
findings.evidence: waterings.py create_watering always INSERTs; the client sends no key

findings.title: Single shared busy flag lets a bed's save be double-submitted
findings.steps: Click 'Save watering' on bed A (slow network), then click 'Water now' on bed B before A finishes, then click A's re-enabled 'Save watering' again
findings.expected: A's button stays disabled until A's request finishes
findings.actual: wateringBedId is one ref: B overwrites it and B's finally sets it to null, so A's button re-enables while A's request is still in flight, and a second click records a duplicate
findings.evidence: beds.vue recordWatering sets wateringBedId.value = bed.id and resets it to null in finally

findings.title: Long unbroken bed names overflow the watering tables at 375 px
findings.steps: Create a bed named with 60 characters and no spaces, record a watering, and view at 375 px wide
findings.actual: The .table cells have no overflow-wrap/word-break and the table has no scroll wrapper, so the 4-column table is wider than the viewport
findings.evidence: main.css has no overflow-wrap/word-break rules; the .table td styles only set padding/alignment

findings.title: Deleted watering ids are reused, so a stale delete can remove a different watering
findings.steps: Delete the newest watering (id 4), record a new one, then retry the old delete (another tab, or a retry after timeout)
findings.actual: The new watering got id 4 again and would be deleted
findings.evidence: DELETE /waterings/4 -> 204, then POST returned {"id":4,...}; the table uses INTEGER PRIMARY KEY without AUTOINCREMENT
